newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to crackdown on illegal literature.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to crackdown on illegal literature.

text.p: Vietnam is set to revive a campaign against social evils this week, which includes raids on bookstores and places suspected of selling or issuing illegal literature, a government official said on Monday.

The official, who declined to be named, told Reuters the measure was being discussed at a government meeting in Ho Chi Minh City on Monday and Tuesday aimed at completing plans for a broader pre-lunar new year crackdown on social vices.
"...Raids will be carried out where publications are being circulated illegally, with Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City being the prime grounds," he said.
He added that the campaign would target problems such as pornography but would focus on underground literature aimed at undermining the socialist government and government policy.

Tan Lai Khieu, chief inspector at the Culture Ministry, said in an interview published at the weekend that raids were being planned this week on bars, restaurants, karaoke rooms, video shops and dance halls.

He added, however, that Hanoi was hoping to avoid the mistakes of a drive against social evils last year in which police teams swept through the nation's cities tearing down and destroying signboards bearing foreign brand names.
The move sent shockwaves through Vietnam's multi-billion dollar foreign investment community, prompting a backdown by government officials who blamed the move on over-zealous police enforcement.
Western analysts say Hanoi is concerned about anti-government literature, particularly a recent newsletter known as the Nguoi Saigon (Saigonese), which circulates both inside the country and abroad.
Some of these publications are said to have the tacit backing of high-level officials.
This year's Tet lunar new year festival is due to be celebrated on and around February 6.
